The REIT will also enter several other broad-based indices, potentially increasing its visibility and participation from institutional and passive investors. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-133180560,width-210,height-158,imgsize-210836,resizemode-75/embassy-office-parks-reit-to-enter-nifty-500-become-only-investment-trust-in-nifty-midcap-150br.jpg"> Agencies Embassy REIT to enter Nifty 500, Nifty Midcap 150 from September 30 Embassy Office Parks REIT , India’s first listed REIT and the largest office REIT in Asia, will be included in the Nifty 500 and Nifty Midcap 150 as part of the latest periodic review by NSE Indices Limited. The revised index composition will come into effect from September 30, 2026. Embassy REIT will be the only REIT included in the Nifty Midcap 150 under the new composition. The inclusion will also see Embassy REIT added to several other broad-based NSE indices, expanding its presence across key market benchmarks. In addition to the Nifty 500 and Nifty Midcap 150, Embassy REIT will be included in the Nifty Next 100, Nifty LargeMidcap 250, Nifty MidSmallcap 400 and Nifty Total Market indices. Its inclusion in the Nifty 500 will also extend to the Nifty500 Equal Weight, Nifty500 Multicap and Nifty500 LargeMidSmall Equal-Cap Weighted indices. Embassy REIT said its inclusion across these indices broadens its visibility across the investment universe and creates the potential for greater participation from institutional and passive investors . The company noted that the Nifty Midcap 150 is already tracked by multiple ETFs and index funds in India, making its inclusion in the index particularly relevant from an investor access perspective. Live Events Amit Shetty, Chief Executive Officer of Embassy REIT, said the inclusion in the Nifty 500 and, notably, as the only REIT in the Nifty Midcap 150, marks a significant moment for the company and the continued evolution of India's listed REIT market. According to Shetty, index inclusion brings REITs further into the mainstream of India's capital markets and enables access to a broader pool of investors. Embassy REIT is India's first listed REIT and has played a pioneering role in the growth of the asset class, Shetty said. He added that the company remains focused on delivering sustained performance and long-term value for its unitholders. Shares of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) tumbled around 4% on Wednesday, recording the biggest single day plunge in more than two months after Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran resigned. The shares of India’s largest IT services provider closed at around Rs 2,350 apiece on NSE, wiping off around Rs 35,000 crore from its market capitalisation and dragging it down to Rs 8.5 lakh crore. It closed as the top loser on benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty, as well as sectoral index Nifty IT which it pulled down 1.5%, making it the top sectoral loser. N Chandrasekaran on Wednesday resigned as Tata Sons Chairman, after one Board member did not support the proposal to extend his tenure. The Economic Times was the first to break the development this morning. Chandrasekaran’s current tenure as chairman of Tata Sons ends on February 20 next year. “Tata Sons is a very large institution and there are many strategic projects that are under critical stages of execution,” he said. “It is not only necessary to have a leader in place to lead the Group beyond Feb 2027, but also clarity on leadership is important for employees, investors, partners and other stakeholders…Under these circumstances, earlier today, I have communicated to the Tata Sons Board, that I have decided not to offer myself for reappointment when my term ends,” he added. Following this, the shares of salt-to-airlines conglomerate Tata Group companies sharply tumbled. TCS, which has the largest market capitalisation in the Tata pack, recorded the sharpest decline in the pack. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-133185966,width-210,height-158,imgsize-22744,resizemode-75/indiqube-spaces-q1-revenue-jumps-37-to-record-rs-428-crorebr.jpg"> Agencies IndiQube delivered record quarterly revenue and strong profit growth in Q1FY27, supported by higher occupancy, expanding workspace capacity and rising contribution from value-added services. Integrated managed spaces platform IndiQube Spaces Limited , has reported its highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs 428 crore, reflecting 37% YoY growth for Q1FY27. “EBITDA increased 34% to Rs 87 crore, EBIT grew 59% to Rs 55 crore, and PAT grew 91% to Rs 35 crore. EBITDA margins remained healthy at 20%, while EBIT and PAT margins improved to 13% and 8% respectively, demonstrating the operating leverage inherent in our platform as we continue to scale. With this momentum, we remain focused on maintaining a healthy balance of scale, profitability & capital efficiency,” said Rishi Das, Cofounder & CEO, IndiQube. Company’s area under management increased by 1.91 million sq. ft YoY, to 10.61 million sq. ft while seat capacity increased by 43,000 seats to 236,000 seats. “Our operating performance in Q1 FY27 reflects the increasing depth and efficiency of the IndiQube platform. Steady state occupancy strengthened to 90% and overall occupancy improved to 86%, underscoring healthy customer demand and improved utilization across the portfolio,” said Meghna Agarwal, Co-founder, IndiQube. Value Added Services also continued to scale rapidly, with VAS revenue reaching Rs 72 crore and its contribution to operating revenue increasing from 11% to 17%. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-133185397,width-210,height-158,imgsize-12698,resizemode-75/pilani-investment-to-sell-1-7-million-ultratech-cement-shares-for-1908-crorebr.jpg"> Agencies Pilani Investment to sell 1.7M UltraTech Cement shares for ₹1,908 cr, while UltraTech acquires a 26% stake in Solaris Horizon Energy. Pilani Investment and Industries Corporation is set to sell approximately 1.7 million equity shares of UltraTech Cement through a vendor sale on the screen-based trading platforms of Indian stock exchanges, with the trade expected to take place on Thursday, August 13, 2026. The offer represents approximately 0.57% of UltraTech Cement’s existing total outstanding equity shares, based on shareholding available on the BSE for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, according to the deal term documents. The books opened on August 12 and are scheduled to close on August 13 at around 7:30 a.m. IST, with an option to close earlier. The expected trade date is August 13, with settlement expected to take place on August 14. ALSO READ: Lenskart Q1 Results: Profit zooms 182% YoY to Rs 228 crore; revenue up 34% The offer floor price has been set at Rs 11,481 per equity share, representing a 3% discount to UltraTech Cement’s last closing price of Rs 11,836 on the BSE as of August 12. At the offer floor price, the transaction is valued at approximately Rs 1,908.5 crore, or about $200 million. Live Events The transaction is 100% secondary, with Pilani Investment and Industries Corporation as the seller. Jefferies India Private Limited is the sole bookrunner and sole broker for the transaction. The transaction carries a 60-day lock-up. The transaction is being offered to institutional investors and is not for distribution to retail clients. “No pricing guidance will be provided until the equity shares are crossed on the Indian stock exchanges on August 13. Investors are required to indicate demand sensitivities across the price range,” the deal term documents said. UltraTech eyes 26% stake in Solaris Horizon Energy In another development, UltraTech Cement has informed the exchanges that it has entered into an Energy Supply Agreement and Share Subscription and Shareholders Agreement to acquire a 26% equity stake in Solaris Horizon Energy Private Limited, a company engaged in the generation and transmission of renewable energy . “The acquisition is for the purposes of meeting the Company’s green energy needs, optimising energy cost and comply with regulatory requirements for captive power consumption under electricity laws,” UltraTech Cement said in an exchange filing on August 12. This strategic shift is designed to enhance compliance and streamline processes within the standardized framework, ensuring that price variations tied to a Z-score of five facilitate a more accessible business environment for market participants. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-133185219,width-210,height-158,imgsize-67822,resizemode-75/sebi-lowers-stress-testing-limit-for-commodity-derivativesbr.jpg"> Agencies Markets regulator Sebi on Wednesday lowered the Z-score limit used for stress testing in the commodity derivatives market to 5 from 10, in a move aimed at easing compliance for market participants. Under the existing framework, price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 10 replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has now revised the provision to a Z-score of 5, according to its circular. The regulator said, "Price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 5 will replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities. Mean and sigma of returns over the applicable MPOR period across 15 years would be used for calculation of the Z-score." The change applies to the standardised stress testing framework prescribed under the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund (Core SGF) for commodity derivatives. Live Events The earlier provision stated, "Price movements corresponding to a Z-score of 10 will replace extreme price movements beyond that threshold in peak historical returns of all commodities." Sebi said the modification has been made "with the objective of facilitating Ease of Doing Business ". The revised circular comes into force with immediate effect. The move relates to the historical scenarios used for peak historical return stress testing, under which the maximum percentage rise and fall in the price of each underlying over the Margin Period of Risk (MPOR) during the last 15 years are considered. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-133184673,width-210,height-158,imgsize-52114,resizemode-75/mcx-nism-launch-centre-to-strengthen-indias-commodity-market-skillsbr.jpg"> ETMarkets.com MCX and NISM are joining forces to build commodity market expertise through specialised training, research and investor awareness, supporting India’s evolving derivatives ecosystem. Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd. ( MCX ) and the National Institute of Securities Markets ( NISM ) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at the Global Commodity Conclave 2026 to establish the MCX-NISM Centre for Commodity Markets , a dedicated platform focused on strengthening professional capability, research and responsible participation in India’s commodity markets. Housed at NISM, it will combine MCX’s industry and market expertise with NISM’s academic infrastructure and research capabilities. As India’s commodity markets become more sophisticated and globally integrated, the initiative fulfils a need for specialised skills, research, and market awareness. The core focus areas include capacity building and professional development, applied research, investor awareness , and academic engagement. Its programmes will be helpful for market participants, corporates, investors and the wider academic community. It will emphasise practical knowledge and informed participation. The key objective is to sharpen the understanding of commodity derivatives and their role in managing market risks. The training programmes will cover multiple issues, including hedging , corporate risk management , ethical conduct, suitability, compliance and good market practices. It will also conduct research and draft policy and white papers. A slew of faculty development programmes, doctoral fellowships, visiting scholar initiatives, and academic symposia will help build a sustained talent pipeline. Live Events MCX will contribute its domain expertise and aid in content development, instructional design and assessment development, helping break down market knowledge into structured learning programmes with clear outcomes. Sashi Krishnan, Director, National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM) said, “The development of commodity markets rests on research that is rigorous, current, and grounded in the realities of the Indian market as well as on a steady supply of well-trained professionals. NISM's mandate is centred on capacity building for the securities markets. As commodity trading grows more intr.icate, with new products, wider market linkages, and a regulatory framework that continues to evolve, the case for dedicated research only grows stronger. The issue will open on August 18 and close on August 31, with an option for early closure. Proceeds will fund onward lending, refinancing existing debt, and general corporate purposes. Agencies Indel Money, a non-deposit taking non-banking finance company, on Wednesday said it proposes to raise up to Rs 500 crore through public issue of non-convertible debentures (NCDs) of face value of Rs 1,000 each. The issue opens on August 18 and closes on August 31 with an option of early closure, subject to relevant approvals, Indel Money said in a statement. Investors may make one or more applications for the NCDs, subject to a minimum application size of Rs 10,000 across all series collectively and in multiples of Rs 1,000 thereafter, it said. Bonds Corner Powered By India bonds flat, major move likely only after US inflation data Indian government bonds remained mostly stable on Wednesday, with traders eyeing important US inflation statistics expected later that day. The local retail inflation for July edged up to 4.45 percent, while oil prices declined slightly following news of a ceasefire extension. Overnight index swap rates showed little change, reflecting expectations surrounding the upcoming US economic data. Apollo Hospitals Enterprise on Wednesday, August 12, reported a 38.4% year-on-year (YoY) jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 610 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1FY27), compared with Rs 441 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Revenue from operations rose 20.6% YoY to Rs 7,044 crore in Q1FY27, compared with Rs 5,842 crore in the year-ago period, according to the company's exchange filing. The healthcare major's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 28.2% YoY to Rs 1,092 crore from Rs 852 crore in Q1FY26. The EBITDA margin also improved to 15.5% from 14.6% a year earlier. Ahead of the results, Apollo Hospitals shares settled 1.72% lower at Rs 8,597 apiece on the NSE on Wednesday. Apollo Health and Lifestyle reported a 15% YoY increase in revenue to Rs 499 crore. Apollo HealthCo reported revenue of Rs 2,977 crore, while EBITDA stood at Rs 171 crore. The company said revenue growth was driven by higher volumes in its specialties and an increase in high-complexity clinical work. Capacity Expansion Apollo Hospitals continued its capacity expansion during the quarter with the launch of a 180-bed hospital in Sarjapur, Bengaluru. The company's Gurugram facility remains on track for commissioning in Q3FY27. The company also announced plans to expand its existing hospital facilities in Indore and Guwahati by 148 beds. In addition, Apollo plans to add four new hospitals in Indore, Dwarka, Delhi Proton Centre and Ranchi, with a combined capacity of around 1,200 beds. With these additions, Apollo Hospitals plans to add more than 5,000 beds, including 4,700 census beds, over the next five years.
